question: Explain backtracking using subsets and permutations. How does pruning help?

scenes.sub: Try a choice, explore everything after it, undo it, try the next.
scenes.say: Backtracking is how you generate every subset, permutation, or combination. The pattern is always the same three moves, and it's easy to remember with a pizza.

scenes.head: Pizza with two toppings
scenes.say: Build a pizza from two toppings, olive and onion. Start with a plain pizza. Write it down. Add olive: write it down. Add onion on top: write it down. Now the key move. Next, take the onion off. Then take the olive off too. Try onion alone: write it down. Four pizzas, every possible subset. Backtracking is: choose, explore everything after it, then undo.

scenes.head: Subsets in code
scenes.say: Cur is the pizza we're building. Every call writes the current pizza into res. Then loop over the toppings from position i onward. First choose: push a topping. Then explore: recurse with j plus one, so we only look at later toppings and never repeat a subset. Finally undo: pop it off, restoring cur exactly as before. For n items that's two to the n subsets, so O of n times two to the n.

scenes.head: Permutations: order matters
scenes.say: For permutations, order matters, so every call may pick any item, not just later ones. We need a used array to avoid picking the same item twice. When the path is complete, save it. Otherwise try each unused item: mark it used, push it, recurse. Then undo both. For one, two, three that gives six permutations. In general, n factorial times n.

scenes.head: Pruning: stop dead branches early
scenes.say: Pruning means abandoning a branch the moment it cannot work. Target seven from two, three, six, seven, reusing numbers. If a candidate is bigger than what's left, break, because the list is sorted and everything after it is bigger too. Passing j, not j plus one, allows reuse. Answers: two two three, and seven. Without the break, we'd explore thousands of hopeless paths on larger inputs. Classics: Subsets, Permutations, Combination Sum, N Queens.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: Subsets O of n times two to the n. Permutations O of n times n factorial.
Sort first, then skip a[j] equal to a[j-1] at the same level.
If subproblems overlap, memoize; otherwise enumerate with pruning.
Forgetting the undo step, so cur leaks into other branches.
scenes.say: Follow-ups. Complexity: exponential, so n times two to the n for subsets, n times n factorial for permutations. Duplicates? Sort, then skip equal neighbours at the same level. Backtracking versus D P? Memoize when subproblems overlap. The common mistake: forgetting the undo, so one branch leaks into another.

lines: Prune any branch that cannot lead to an answer.
Cost is exponential, so always say the limit on n.
scenes.say: Backtracking is choose, explore, undo. Prune any branch that cannot lead to an answer. The cost is exponential, so always mention how small n has to be.
